# Your first plot

Time to make a plot. We'll start with an easy question so we can learn the one idea
behind *every* ggplot as we go — the **grammar of graphics**.

> **Question:** what does our experiment look like — how many samples are there in
> each lifestyle?

The plot that answers it is a simple **bar chart**. Building it teaches the grammar we'll
reuse all day.

## data → aesthetics → geom {-}

Every ggplot needs three things:

- **data** — the table to plot (`meta`)
- **aesthetics** (`aes`) — which column maps to what (here: `lifestyle` → x-axis)
- **geom** — how to draw it (here: bars)

```{r}
ggplot(meta, aes(x = lifestyle)) +   # data + aesthetic
  geom_bar()                         # geom: one bar per group
```

That's a complete answer: how many samples per lifestyle. 🎉

## Add a layer: another aesthetic {-}

Plots grow by adding more with `+`. Map a **second** variable to the `fill` aesthetic to
also see the timepoints:

```{r}
ggplot(meta, aes(x = lifestyle, fill = timepoint)) +
  geom_bar()
```

## Add labels {-}

`labs()` makes it readable:

```{r}
ggplot(meta, aes(x = lifestyle, fill = timepoint)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Our experiment", x = NULL, y = "Number of samples", fill = "Timepoint")
```

<div class="remember">
  <strong>📌 The grammar, once and for all:</strong> <code>ggplot(data, aes(...))</code>
  sets the data and the mappings, then you add <code>geom_*()</code> and other layers
  with <code>+</code>. Change the <em>aesthetic</em> or the <em>geom</em> and you change
  the plot — that's all of ggplot.
</div>

### 👉 Your turn {-}

Answer a flipped version of the question: make a bar chart with **`timepoint`** on the
x-axis, filled by **`lifestyle`**, with nice labels.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>
```{r, eval=FALSE}
ggplot(meta, aes(x = timepoint, fill = lifestyle)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Number of samples", fill = "Lifestyle")
```
</details>

> 🤖 **Ask your AI:** *"In ggplot2, what's the difference between mapping `fill` inside
> `aes()` and setting `fill = "blue"` outside it?"*
